record.original_question: Consider Combinatory Logic extended with Boolean constants T and F and a conditional constant C, with rules I x -> x, K x y -> x, S x y z -> (x z)(y z), C T x y -> x, C F x y -> y, and the semi-equational rule that x is convertible to y implies C z x y -> x. Is this nonterminating semi-equational conditional rewrite system confluent?

evidence.quote: Is the extension of Combinatory Logic by Boolean constants confluent?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider Combinatory Logic extended with two Boolean constants $T$ and $F$ and a ternary conditional constant $C$. Terms are built from variables and the constants $I, K, S, T, F, C$ by left-associative application. Define a conditional rewrite system with the following rules:

(1) $I\,x \to x$,
(2) $K\,x\,y \to x$,
(3) $S\,x\,y\,z \to (x\,z)(y\,z)$,
(4) $C\,T\,x\,y \to x$,
(5) $C\,F\,x\,y \to y$,
(6) the semi-equational conditional rule: if $x$ is convertible to $y$ (i.e.\ $x \leftrightarrow^{*} y$ in the system itself), then $C\,z\,x\,y \to x$.

Here ``semi-equational'' means the side condition $x \leftrightarrow^{*} y$ uses the symmetric-transitive closure of the rewrite relation, and the system is nonterminating. Determine whether this rewrite system is confluent: that is, whether for every term $t$ and all reductions $t \to^{*} u$ and $t \to^{*} v$ there exists a term $w$ with $u \to^{*} w$ and $v \to^{*} w$.
artifact.status_search_result: The confluence of this system (RTA open problem 15) was established by Ł. Czajka in "Confluence of an extension of Combinatory Logic by Boolean constants" (arXiv:1306.2069, FSCD 2017), with a Coq formalization available. The system is confirmed confluent.
